status: REGISTERED 2026-11-18: frozen BEFORE any budget number was computed (only a timing check on the hourly grid, values not printed). Hashes in long_prereg_budget.sha256. Later changes only as dated addenda.
approval: Parts 1 and 2 of the five-part plan ('how big' and 'which pitfall'). Student's words, 2026-11-18: 'I approve of the 5 parts'.
questions: Part 1: how large an apparent quantum advantage does each evaluation pitfall produce on copper, compared with what the same selection produces when neither model is better?
Part 2: starting from a sound protocol, how much of the apparent advantage under a protocol with all pitfalls does each pitfall contribute (Shapley decomposition), and how do they stack?
data: Saved intraday forecasts only (long_preds_dom, dom2, dom3, dom4; per-seed arrays seedp_*), grids F, M, H, test years 2014-2025 (2013 only to pick the 2014 reference). 2026 is not read. Daily is not included (no per-seed daily forecasts). No model is trained. Seed lottery: hourly_databento_preds_v5 seeds2_QLSTMT_h16 and seeds2_LSTM_h5, 50 seeds each.
design: budget_lib.py docstring (six factors SEED, WINDOW, GRID, LOSS, QMODEL, REF; control and pitfall definitions; apparent ratio = minimum over the options a protocol leaves open; 64 protocols; Shapley on log ratio; week-swap null with flips shared across grids, B = 200, seeds 41000+b, for the 32 protocols with REF = control). Seed lottery: 2000 random draws of k seeds per model, k in {1,3,5,10,25}, seed 42000.
why_these_pitfalls: They are the ones the pilot prevalence coding (PROGRESS/30d) found most often in published QML forecasting papers that can be re-enacted on saved forecasts: few or selected seeds (81%), a single test window (78%), choice of metric, reporting the best setting, and a weak baseline (81% without a naive/strong benchmark). Test-period selection of reservoir instances and features is the companion Li et al. audit's result and is NOT re-counted here.

decision_rules.single_selection_pitfall: Observed apparent advantage vs the null: if observed >= null 5th percentile of the ratio (i.e. the advantage is not beyond the null 95th percentile), 'within what selection alone produces'; else 'beyond what selection alone produces'.
decision_rules.all_selection: The same rule for the protocol with all five selection pitfalls (REF control); headline wording: 'the apparent advantage is no larger than selection alone produces when neither model is better' or '... exceeds ...'.
decision_rules.REF: Systematic, not a selection: reported as the change in apparent advantage from control, no null.
decision_rules.decomposition: Shapley values of the log ratio from control to all six pitfalls, reported in points and as shares of the total. If a factor's Shapley value is positive (it reduces apparent advantage), that is reported as such.
decision_rules.seed_lottery: Reported descriptively: for each k the median ratio, 5-95% range, and P(ratio < 1), P(ratio < 0.97), P(ratio > 1.03), next to the 50-seed ratio.

claude_prediction_recorded_for_transpare.text: Control ratio about 1.00 to 1.02 (DOM slightly worse than a past-selected classical model). All six pitfalls together: apparent advantage 3 to 6%. Largest Shapley shares: REF (weak untuned ESN) and WINDOW (best test year); SEED small at intraday sample sizes; LOSS moderate. All-selection observed advantage within the null 95th percentile. Seed lottery: at k = 3, P(ratio < 0.97) around 0.1-0.3.

known_limits: The week-swap null makes the two models exchangeable; it assumes the pitfall procedure acts the same under the null.
The 'researcher' is assumed to choose the best-looking option; real papers may choose less aggressively, so the budget is an upper bound on what each choice can produce.
The REF pitfall uses one weak reference (ESN28u).
AI-written code not re-derived by the student.
cost_estimate: Tables: about 2 minutes; observed: seconds; null: about 10-20 minutes; seed lottery: under a minute.
stop_rule: One run, report, stop. No further factors, options, losses, nulls or references after results.
